references.text: Samson goes down to Timnah again and speaks with the woman, showing his continued interest in the Philistine woman he first saw.
The daughters of the Philistines are mentioned again in connection with Samson's marriage to the Timnite woman.
Abraham warned against taking a wife from the daughters of the Canaanites, which stands in contrast to Samson's choice of a Philistine woman.
Judah also went down and saw a Canaanite woman whom he took as his wife, a similar pattern to Samson who went down to Timnah and saw a woman.
The Mosaic law forbade marriage with the pagan peoples, including to prevent Israel from being led away from the Lord.
Samson continues his pattern of being attracted to Philistine women, this time in Gaza.
Samson's attraction to Delilah, another Philistine woman, follows the same pattern as his interest in the woman in Timnah.
